name: Refugee Status (Condición de Refugiado, COMAR)

qualifying_event.description: A person who fears returning to their country of origin due to persecution or serious harm may apply for refugee status through COMAR (Comisión Mexicana de Ayuda a Refugiados), physically present in Mexico.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Identity documents if available; evidence supporting the persecution/harm claim.

requirements.blocker_text: Must apply at a COMAR office (Mexico City, Tapachula, Palenque, Tenosique, Oluta, Guadalajara, Tijuana, Saltillo, or Monterrey) within 30 working days of arrival in Mexico, or via INM/a migration station where no local COMAR office exists.

evidence_required.document: Application filed in person at a COMAR office within the 30-working-day window
Identity/supporting documentation for the protection claim

outcome.duration_length: not specified in sources reviewed for the processing period itself; recognized refugees receive permanent residence directly

sources.title: UNHCR Mexico -- How to apply for refugee status in Mexico (COMAR): offices, 30-day deadline, work authorisation, outcome

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Mexico's initial build. STATUS SET TO DRAFT: sourced from UNHCR Mexico (tier 2) rather than a Mexican government source -- a COMAR government page (gob.mx/comar/articulos/requisitos-para-solicitar-refugio-en-mexico) was located and is almost certainly the right tier-1 source, but it returned an HTTP 403 to automated fetching in this pass and so could not be read and cited directly; flagged here rather than silently substituted. Mexico's asylum system has grown rapidly into one of the world's largest by application volume, driven heavily by transiting/Central American and other claimants. Per UNHCR: applicants get a CONSTANCIA on filing, then may separately apply to INM for a Visitor Card for Humanitarian Reasons (TVRH) that permits work while the claim is processed -- work_rights set 'full' reflects this authorised-work provision during processing as well as post-recognition, not merely the recognized-refugee end state. Notably generous outcome: recognized refugees (and included family members) reportedly receive PERMANENT residence directly -- not a temporary-then-upgrade path as in many other countries in this dataset -- but this specific point also awaits tier-1 confirmation.
